heading: JPG Compressor Online to Reduce Photo File Size
introduction:
JPG images are used across websites, online stores, social media, email attachments and digital documents. Their ability to store detailed photographs in relatively small files makes them a popular choice for everyday image sharing.

However, some JPG photographs are still too large for a particular purpose. An online form may have a maximum upload limit, an email attachment may exceed the allowed size, or a website may need smaller images to reduce page weight.

The File Compresser JPG Compressor helps reduce the size of JPG and JPEG photographs directly in your browser. You can choose between different quality modes, set a maximum target size and compare the actual output with your original photograph.

sections.heading: Keep a copy of your original JPG
sections.body: Add the photograph and review the default Balanced mode for a moderate quality trade-off. Compare faces, textures and text at the same scale. High quality retains more detail at a potentially larger size; Maximum is an optional stronger mode that prioritizes smaller output with a greater risk of visible artifacts.

sections.heading: A target size is a limit, not an exact byte count
sections.body: Target size searches actual encodes and verifies the final byte count. A 50 KB maximum means 50,000 bytes, not a promise of exactly that size. If no supported encode fits, the result is marked Target not met. Image dimensions stay unchanged.

sections.heading: Where JPG works well
sections.body: JPG suits photographs and many opaque web images. It cannot preserve transparency. Inspect faces, fine textures and lettering, and keep the camera or design original because repeated lossy encoding can add artifacts.
